newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Juncker sees stability pact deal in Dublin.
newsitem.headline: Juncker sees stability pact deal in Dublin.

text.p: European Union finance ministers will probably bury differences over the single currency stability pact in time for a deal to be presented to Friday's Dublin summit, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said in an interview with newspaper Luxemburger Wort.

"My feeling is that the finance ministers meeting on Thursday evening in Dublin will wrap up the stability pact in time to put it on the summit agenda," Juncker, who is also Luxembourg's finance minister, said.
"But in any case it would not be a catastrophe if we have to wait to next June's Amsterdam summit to definitively adopt it."

Juncker said he doubted the stability pact would result in automatic fines being imposed on countries in the economic and monetary union (EMU) whose deficits exceed three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
But he said any breach of the deficit target should lead to the automatic start of a sanctions procedure that could result in fines. This was, however, ultimately a political decision.
